celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿لَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) in both places ﴿أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ﴾ which blames itself even if it has striven hard in doing good. The answer to the oath is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected", indicated by:

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ i.e. the unbeliever ﴿أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ﴾ for the resurrection and bringing back to life?

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ We will gather them, ﴿قَادِرِينَ﴾ along with gathering them, ﴿عَلَى أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾ which is the fingers, i.e. We restore their bones as they were despite their smallness, so how much more the large ones?

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ﴾ the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and it is in the accusative by an implied أَنْ, i.e. to deny ﴿أَمَامَهُ﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُ أَيَّانَ﴾ when ﴿يَوْمُ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ a question of mockery and denial.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَإِذَا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ﴾ with kasra on the rāʾ and with fatḥa; it is dazed and bewildered at what it sees of what it used to deny,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ﴾ darkens and its light goes,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ﴾ so they rise from the west, or their light goes; and that is on the Day of Resurrection,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿يَقُولُ الْإِنْسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ﴾ the fleeing.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent from seeking to flee; ﴿لَا وَزَرَ﴾ no refuge in which to fortify oneself.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ﴾ the resting place of all creatures, and they are reckoned and recompensed.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يُنَبَّأُ الْإِنْسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ﴾ of the first of his deeds and the last of them.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾ a witness: his limbs speak of his deeds; the hāʾ [i.e. tāʾ marbūṭa] is for intensiveness; so his recompense is inevitable,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَلْقَى مَعَاذِيرَهُ﴾ plural of مَعْذِرَة, irregularly; i.e. even if he brought every excuse, it would not be accepted from him. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet:

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ﴾ with the Quran, before Gabriel has finished it, ﴿لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ﴾ for fear that it escapes you.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ﴾ in your breast ﴿وَقُرْآنَهُ﴾ your reciting it, i.e. its flowing on your tongue.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ﴾ to you, by Gabriel's recitation, ﴿فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ﴾ listen to his recitation; so he ﷺ would listen and then recite it.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ﴾ by making you understand. The connection between this ayah and what precedes it is that that one involved turning away from Allah's signs, and this one involves hastening to them by memorising them.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an opening particle (istiftāḥ) in the sense of أَلَا; ﴿بَلْ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ﴾ this world; with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تُحِبُّونَ] in both verbs,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ and so do not work for it [وَتَذَرُونَ].

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ i.e. on the Day of Resurrection ﴿نَاضِرَةٌ﴾ beautiful and radiant,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ﴾ i.e. they will see Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿تَظُنُّ﴾ are certain ﴿أَنْ يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾ a great calamity that breaks the vertebrae (faqār) of the back.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ in the sense of أَلَا; ﴿إِذَا بَلَغَتِ﴾ the soul ﴿التَّرَاقِيَ﴾ the bones of the throat,

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ those around him say: ﴿مَنْ رَاقٍ﴾ to recite incantations over him so that he may be cured?

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَظَنَّ﴾ the one whose soul has reached that is certain ﴿أَنَّهُ الْفِرَاقُ﴾ parting from this world,

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ﴾ i.e. one of his legs with the other at death; i.e. the hardship of parting from this world is entwined with the hardship of the Hereafter's approach;

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُ﴾ i.e. the driving; this indicates what governs إِذَا; the meaning is: when the soul reaches the throat, it is driven to the judgement of its Lord.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿فَلَا صَدَّقَ﴾ the human being ﴿وَلَا صَلَّى﴾ i.e. he did not believe and did not pray,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى﴾ strutting in his walk out of self-admiration.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿أَوْلَى لَكَ﴾ there is in it a shift (iltifāt) from the third person; the word is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), and the lām is for clarification; i.e. may what you hate befall you; ﴿فَأَوْلَى﴾ i.e. for it is more fitting for you than for anyone else.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾ thinks ﴿الْإِنْسَانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدًى﴾ neglected, not charged with the laws? I.e. he should not think that.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ﴾ i.e. he was ﴿نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ تُمْنَى﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يُمْنَى], poured into the womb,

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ﴾ the semen ﴿عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ﴾ Allah from it the human being ﴿فَسَوَّى﴾ proportioned his limbs,

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ﴾ from the semen that became a clinging clot, i.e. a piece of blood, then a chewed lump, i.e. a piece of flesh, ﴿الزَّوْجَيْنِ﴾ the two kinds, ﴿الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى﴾ they sometimes come together and sometimes each one comes alone without the other.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ﴾ the doer of these things ﴿بِقَادِرٍ عَلَى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَى﴾ He ﷺ said: "Yes indeed."
